newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Bid to scrap Tanzania coffee auction doomed.
newsitem.headline: Bid to scrap Tanzania coffee auction doomed.

text.p: A proposal by German coffee trading company Mazao Ltd for replacing Tanzania's coffee auction system appears unlikely to materialise, government and industry sources said on Friday.
A Mazao Ltd delegate to Tanzania's annual coffee industry meeting proposed on Wednesday a fully-liberalised system with buyers purchasing coffee direct from farmers.
The delegate argued this would result in faster export marketing.
"I have to sell my coffee as soon as possible after purchase to eliminate any risks (price fluctuation)," the delegate said.
But traders said while they might support changes to the auction system it was the best instrument currently available earning the government valuable foreign exchange.

"The auction is a very important tool at the moment. The coffee auction is a major earner of foreign exchange (and) is the best tool right now because it provides a transparent price," said one trader who asked not to be named.
Tanzania's twice-monthly coffee auction is held in Moshi and acts as the main point of transaction between growers and exporters.
Scrapping the auction system would require an act of parliament and approval by cabinet, said Tanzania Coffee Board (TCB) managing director, Edward Sannda.

"The (East African) countries with auction systems come way ahead of anyone else in terms of returns to farmers. The highest payment to the farmers has always come from those countries with the auction system," Sannda said.
Kenya and Tanzania both have coffee auctions.
Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Paul Kimiti said some aspects of the auction may need to be reviewed as competition moved from the auction to the village buying post.

"If changes to the auction system are perceived necessary by the industry, I request the industry and TCB to set up a taskforce to look into this issue and come up with proposals, even before the next crop season," Kimiti said.
